value.loc: 4. Main Result, Theorem 4.1, p.7; 5. Committee Selection, Theorem 5.1, p.10
value.quote: under Assumption 1, there exists a 6.24-approximate core solution.
value.note: Main results are existence of outcomes in the gamma-approximate (proportional) core, a fairness property; the approximation factor relaxes a property rather than approximating an optimum of a welfare objective, so WD is not coded. Algorithms are constructive proof devices and the conclusion puts computational aspects beyond scope, so AL is not coded.

C1.reason: The gamma-approximate core is a relaxed proportionality property, not performance against a welfare/distortion objective, so the results are axiomatic (AX) only.

value.loc: 2. Notations and Preliminaries, p.3; 5. Committee Selection, Def. 5.1-5.2 and Sec. 5.1, p.10
value.quote: Note that both ranking and approval preferences may allow ties.
value.note: General model: strict preference orders over outcomes ('We assume that the order is strict'). Section 5: ranking preferences induced by an item ranking and approval preferences given by an approved set Mi; the induced preferences over committees may have ties (weak orders). No input format outside the listed codes, so OTH is not needed.

C2.2.reason: The general model uses strict orders (RANK), Section 5 uses approval sets (APPR) and explicitly allows ties in the induced committee preferences (WEAK), while B's OTH describes strict orders already covered by RANK.

value.quote_behav: preference order ⪰i over O. We assume that the order is strict.
value.note: Voters' preferences are the exogenous, fixed input to the outcome selection, which C6 counts as a fixed action; the LEO demand choices (Sec. 3.2) are a proof device, not voting behaviour, so not STRAT.

C6.VOT.reason: C6 counts types whose actions are fixed by the model, and voters supplying their exogenous preferences to the rule is such a fixed (non-strategic, implicitly sincere) action, consistent with C3.1 = NONE.
